title: Grantor can read and write the grantee's account notes
description: An authenticated account creates a directional link that names another account as grantee. links_grant treats that row as authority in both directions, so the grantor can list and create notes on the grantee's account. The grantee does not approve the link.
root_cause: links_grant authorizes a caller when either account is the grantor. The second disjunct matches a link the caller created, with the caller as grantor and the target account as grantee. may_read_account uses that result for both listing and creating notes.
intended_behavior: A link lets the grantee read and create notes on the grantor's account only. The grantor does not gain the grantee's notes, and the grantee does not gain any account except the grantor.

trace.description: The grantor calls GET /accounts/{grantee}/notes with their own bearer token.
The caller is not the target account, so the decision is delegated entirely to links_grant.
The second disjunct matches grantor = caller and grantee = target. links_grant returns true and list_notes returns the grantee's note bodies.

evidence.description: The WHERE clause ORs the reverse party order onto the grantor-to-caller direction.
Bind order is (target, caller, caller, target), so the second pair is the caller's own outbound link.
create_note uses the same may_read_account result before inserting a note whose account_id is the path account.
create_link stores the authenticated caller as grantor and the supplied account as grantee with no acceptance step.

conditions.description: The caller has a bearer session for their own active account.
An account_links row has the caller as grantor and the other account as grantee. The caller can create that row through POST /links.

execution.attacker_perspective: Authenticated account that names the victim as grantee.
payloads: POST /accounts/<victim-account-id>/notes Authorization: Bearer <grantor-token> {"body": "note written by the grantor"}
instructions: Create two active accounts and a note on the victim account.
With the other account's token, POST /links naming the victim as grantee_account_id.
GET /accounts/<victim>/notes and POST a note to that same path with the grantor's token.
execution.observed_result: Derived from the source trace: the grantor's GET is authorized because links_grant's second disjunct matches the link the grantor inserted, and the response contains the victim's note bodies. The same helper authorizes POST /accounts/<victim>/notes, which inserts a note stored on the victim account. This is a cross-account read and write.

remediation.strategy: Authorize only an active link whose grantor is the account being accessed and whose grantee is the caller. Remove the reverse disjunct at this decision point.

def links_grant(conn, caller_id, account_id):
    row = conn.execute(
        """
        SELECT id FROM account_links
        WHERE grantor_account_id = ?
          AND grantee_account_id = ?
          AND revoked_at IS NULL
        """,
        (account_id, caller_id),
    ).fetchone()
    return row is not None

likelihood.reason: Any active account can create the link for any other active account id and then call the note routes. No action by the victim is required.

impact.reason: The grantor receives the full note bodies of the grantee and can insert new notes into that account.

confidence.reason: The session lookup, link insert, both note routes, and the SQL bind order are all in the supplied source. A second pass found no later predicate that drops the reverse match.

title: A revoked account link still grants note access
description: The grantor revokes a link by setting revoked_at. links_grant still selects that row, so the grantee can list and create notes on the grantor's account on the next request.
root_cause: links_grant matches only the two account ids. It has no revoked_at IS NULL predicate, while delete_link leaves the row in place and records revocation only in revoked_at.
intended_behavior: Revocation ends the grantee's access on the next request. A revoked link authorizes nothing.

trace.description: After the grantor revokes the link, the grantee calls GET /accounts/{grantor}/notes.
The grantee is not the grantor account, so authorization is the links_grant lookup.
The lookup returns the row whose revoked_at is set. list_notes then returns the grantor's note bodies.

evidence.description: The active-link query predicates are only the grantor and grantee ids.
delete_link sets revoked_at on the existing row and does not delete it.
create_link already treats revoked_at IS NULL as the definition of an active link when checking duplicates.
create_note authorizes the insert with the same helper, so the former grantee can still add notes.

conditions.description: The caller is the grantee and still has their own bearer session.
The account_links row between that grantee and the grantor remains, with revoked_at populated.

execution.attacker_perspective: Former grantee whose link the grantor has revoked.
instructions: Create a link from the grantor to the grantee and a note on the grantor account.
Revoke that link with the grantor's token.
On the next request, list and create notes on the grantor account with the grantee's token.
execution.observed_result: Derived from the source trace: the grantee's next GET /accounts/{grantor}/notes still satisfies links_grant and returns the grantor's note bodies. POST /accounts/{grantor}/notes still inserts a note on the grantor account. This is a cross-account read and write after revocation.

remediation.strategy: Treat a link as authority only when revoked_at IS NULL, using the same active-link predicate create_link already uses for duplicates.

title: Previous device owner keeps access after transfer
description: Transfer changes owner_account_id and inserts a binding for the destination account. The previous owner's binding remains, and device reads and writes treat any binding as current access. The previous owner can still list the device, read and write its readings, and read and write its device notes.
root_cause: may_view_device and devices_for authorize the caller when any device_bindings row exists for that device and account. transfer_device never sets released_at on the previous owner's row, and no query reads released_at.
intended_behavior: After transfer, the previous owner no longer reads or writes the device, its readings, or its notes. Past ownership does not grant access. Only the current owner and current shares can use the device.

trace.description: The previous owner calls GET /devices/{device_id}/readings after the device was transferred.
The caller is no longer owner_account_id. The binding lookup matches the historical device_bindings row and ignores released_at.
may_view_device returns true, so the handler returns every reading on the device now owned by the destination account.

evidence.description: Creating a device inserts a device_bindings row for the original owner with released_at NULL.
transfer_device updates owner_account_id and inserts a new binding. It does not update the previous binding.
devices_for includes a device whenever the caller has any binding row, so the previous owner still sees it in GET /devices.
create_reading uses may_view_device, so the previous owner can insert readings on the transferred device.

conditions.description: The caller is a past owner and still uses that account's bearer session.
A device_bindings row links the past owner to the device. Every successful transfer leaves the original row in place.

execution.attacker_perspective: Previous owner of a device that has been transferred to another account.
instructions: Create a device as account A, record a reading, and transfer the device to account B.
With account A's original token, GET /devices/<device-id>/readings and POST a new reading.
GET /devices with account A's token and observe that the transferred device is still listed.
execution.observed_result: Derived from the source trace: after owner_account_id changes, the previous owner's binding still makes may_view_device return true. GET /devices/{id}/readings returns the device's readings, and POST /devices/{id}/readings writes a reading onto the new owner's device. This is a cross-account read and write. The same gate still admits the previous owner to the device-note routes.

remediation.strategy: On transfer, set released_at on every open binding for the device before inserting the destination binding. Authorize a binding only when released_at IS NULL, in both may_view_device and devices_for.

code_changes.fixed_code:
def may_view_device(conn, caller_id, device_id):
    device = conn.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM devices WHERE id = ?",
        (device_id,),
    ).fetchone()
    if device is None:
        return False
    if int(device["owner_account_id"]) == int(caller_id):
        return True
    binding = conn.execute(
        """
        SELECT id FROM device_bindings
        WHERE device_id = ? AND account_id = ? AND released_at IS NULL
        """,
        (device_id, caller_id),
    ).fetchone()
    if binding is not None:
        return True
    share = conn.execute(
        """
        SELECT id FROM device_shares
        WHERE device_id = ? AND account_id = ?
        """,
        (device_id, caller_id),
    ).fetchone()
    return share is not None


def devices_for(conn, caller_id):
    return conn.execute(
        """
        SELECT DISTINCT d.*
        FROM devices d
        LEFT JOIN device_bindings b
          ON b.device_id = d.id AND b.account_id = ? AND b.released_at IS NULL
        LEFT JOIN device_shares s
          ON s.device_id = d.id AND s.account_id = ?
        WHERE d.owner_account_id = ?
           OR b.id IS NOT NULL
           OR s.id IS NOT NULL
        ORDER BY d.id
        """,
        (caller_id, caller_id, caller_id),
    ).fetchall()


def transfer_device(conn, device_id, to_account_id):
    conn.execute(
        "UPDATE devices SET owner_account_id = ? WHERE id = ?",
        (to_account_id, device_id),
    )
    conn.execute(
        "UPDATE device_bindings SET released_at = ? WHERE device_id = ? AND released_at IS NULL",
        (now(), device_id),
    )
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM device_shares WHERE device_id = ?", (device_id,))
    conn.execute(
        """
        INSERT INTO device_bindings (device_id, account_id, bound_at, released_at)
        VALUES (?, ?, ?, NULL)
        """,
        (device_id, to_account_id, now()),
    )
    conn.commit()

likelihood.reason: Every transfer leaves the original binding, and the previous owner keeps the session they already hold.

impact.reason: The previous owner continues to read the device and its readings and can write new readings and device notes after ownership has moved.

confidence.reason: Binding insert, transfer, and both authorization queries are in the supplied source. A second pass found no write to released_at anywhere in the target.

title: Merge retargets account links onto the survivor
description: When a merge is accepted, links in which the source was grantor or grantee are rewritten so the survivor replaces the source. They stay active. An account the source had granted can then read and create the survivor's notes, including notes the survivor already had. The survivor can read and create notes on accounts that had granted access to the source.
root_cause: accept_merge updates grantee_account_id and grantor_account_id from the source to the survivor and does not set revoked_at. A later may_read_account call treats each rewritten active row as a normal grant.
intended_behavior: Links in which the source was the grantor end, and that grantee does not gain the survivor's notes. Links in which the source was the grantee end, and the survivor does not gain access to accounts that had granted the source. Links the survivor already had stay as they are.

The caller is not the survivor, so note access is decided by links_grant against the link row accept_merge rewrote.

The first disjunct matches grantor = survivor and grantee = caller because accept_merge changed the source's grantor id to the survivor and left revoked_at null. list_notes returns the survivor's note bodies.

evidence.description: The first link update sets grantee_account_id to the survivor wherever the source was the grantee.
The second link update sets grantor_account_id to the survivor wherever the source was the grantor.
create_note uses may_read_account, so each retargeted active link also authorizes inserts.
Source notes are moved onto the survivor before the link rewrite, so the grantee's later list includes those notes and the survivor's older notes.

The later caller is the surviving grantee of a source-granted link, or the survivor using the survivor's own session against an account that had granted the source.

title: A merged account's token acts as the survivor

current() resolves the token through account_for_token and uses the returned row as the caller.
The source row's merged_into_id is set, so the function returns the survivor account. GET /me then serializes the survivor, including recovery_email.

accept_merge sets the source status to merged and stores the survivor id in merged_into_id.
Sessions are inserted at login. No statement in the target deletes or reassigns a session when a merge is accepted.
create_session refuses a new token when status is not active, which leaves already issued source tokens on the substitution path.

The caller presents a token that create_session issued to the source before the merge.

Call GET /me again with that same source token.
